own_solution.law: Energy conservation: f (1/2) m v^2 = m c dT, so dT = f v^2/(2c); T = T0 + dT
assumptions: constant c, no melting, no heat loss in flight (stated)
bullet temperature at the shot equals loading temperature 293 K

T4882.regime: final temperature below the melting point (466 K < 585 K)

T6215.regime: final temperature below the melting point (466 K < 585 K)

notes: dT = 0.5*300^2/(2*130) = 22500/130 = 173.08 K; T = 293 + 173.08 = 466.08 K. With 17 K pre-warming: 483.08 K, still below 585 K. Mass cancels (C). Earlier-day warming is D because the bullet is loaded at 293 K. Variants consistently state 17 K, 8.2 g, 585 K.
